identifier: E. Pretti, H. Zerze, M. Song, Y. Ding, R. Mao, J. Mittal, "Size-dependent thermodynamic structural selection in colloidal crystallization", Science Advances 5(9), eaaw5912 (2019). DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aaw5912. Values entered come from the Results text, the Fig. 1, 2 and 4 captions and Materials and Methods.

publication_status: PEER REVIEWED, CHECKED ON THE FILE. Typeset version of record: submitted 8 January 2019, accepted 12 August 2019, published 13 September 2019.
grade_rule: E3, grade_tag peer_reviewed. Every result is a claim about the MODEL: a two-dimensional 1:1 binary mixture with a short-ranged Fermi-Jagla pair potential, NVT Langevin molecular dynamics in LAMMPS, and free energies of isolated finite crystallites. A second model with explicit DNA strands (in HOOMD-blue) is used only to show the effect is not specific to the pair potential.
license_note: Open access under CC BY-NC 4.0 (AAAS). Identifier, stated conditions and numbers only; nothing of the text, figures or movies is reproduced.
method_as_stated: MAIN ENGINE IS LAMMPS, NOT HOOMD. A and B colloids interact through a Fermi-Jagla pair potential whose parameters are in the Supplementary Text; all molecular dynamics at constant NVT with a Langevin thermostat, in two dimensions. The unlike attraction E_AB is the energy scale; the like attractions are given as E_AA/E_AB and E_BB/E_AB and temperature as kT/E_AB. SELF-ASSEMBLY runs: at least 1,000 particles, 1:1 A:B, number density rho sigma^2 = 0.1 (packing fraction 0.083). ISOLATED CRYSTALLITES: 36, 64, 100, 144, 196, 256 and 324 particles started in square, hexagonal and rhombic arrangements with (10)-type surfaces, 10 replicates per parameter set and start; a state counts as predominant if it holds at least 95% of the total time. STRUCTURE: a similarity parameter between radial distribution functions (simplified from Oganov and Valle), 400 independent g(r) samples per run, bins of 0.01 sigma to 5 sigma, Gaussian smoothing of five bins. FREE ENERGIES: an extension of the Einstein-molecule method to non-periodic crystals with exposed surfaces (one particle fixed, others constrained against rotation), in LAMMPS; kT/E_AB from 0.02 to 0.11 in steps of 0.01; 32-point Gauss-Legendre thermodynamic integration; sizes of at least 36; extrapolation to infinite size linear in 1/sqrt(N) over N >= 100. EXPLICIT-DNA MODEL (Ding and Mittal): 60 single strands (T6C4 and T6G4) per particle with a blending ratio of 0.05, simulated in HOOMD-blue (version not stated) at NVT with a Langevin thermostat and time step 5e-3 sigma m^(1/2) E_AB^(-1/2), confined to a quasi-2D slab between WCA walls 40 sigma apart.
not_entered: The Fermi-Jagla parameters and MD run lengths: in the Supplementary Text, not in the file. Phase boundaries in like-strength versus size and versus temperature (Figs. 2A, 5): figure-only, except the specific transformations and the free-energy crossover the text states. note: Fang et al. 2020 (src_fang_2020_two_step_crystallization) cites this paper as its reference 17 and reaches a compatible picture -- square first, hexagonal once large -- with in-house grand canonical Monte Carlo instead of molecular dynamics. Where the two differ is in what drives it: here the crossover is attributed to size-dependent free energies with surface entropy and heat capacity playing the main role.
